title: tier-2 shipped code: the CDN index page selection and page scan at 0x1424da730

unreachableBranches.why: the page the selection reports is `(hi + lo) / 2` with `0 <= lo <= hi <= pageCount`, so it is never negative; the client's `page < 0` test can only fire for a page count above the 32-bit signed range, which needs an index larger than the emulator's arena

`CdnIndexPageResident` (0x1424da590) returns AL=0 on both whole-file paths (the store at 0x1424da705 and the already-current skip), and this unit's object is always whole-file (`+0x38 == 0`); a non-zero resident status only comes from the streamed branch, which the port does not implement and this unit does not cover

the 6th argument is a 16-byte arena buffer on every case this unit can build (the oracle's pointer slot is an arena address), so the client's null-out_key16 guard is not reachable through the harness's argument surface

notes: SHIPPED-CODE tier-2 unit. The candidate is crates/ow-casc/src/container.rs: select_page (the lower bound with its early equal exit) and decode_page_record (the record scan and the size/offset/key16 decode), built by cargo and called by crates/ow-casc/src/bin/verify_probe.rs through the cdn_index_page_select entry. Production uses both: PageIndex::find_page is select_page and PageIndex::group_lookup / loose_lookup call decode_page_record. The ledger binds the verdict to container.rs + the probe source + the git revision.

Oracle is CdnIndexPageSelect at exe 0x1424da730, 469 bytes (0x1424da730..0x1424da904). Signature: (index*, key*, u8 key_len, u64* out_offset, u32* out_size, u8* out_key16). Arguments 5 and 6 are stack arguments: the client reads them at the caller's [rsp+0x28] and [rsp+0x30], the oracle writes stack arguments there, and fn/EncodingPageIndexSearch, fn/ApplyMoverSettings, fn/BuildMvh, fn/MrnmHandler and fn/MoverStateVector already rely on that. coverageWindow is the whole 469-byte extent, confirmed with the Ghidra bridge by disassembling 0x1424da730..0x1424da905 (the last byte decodes as the JMP of the found path).

The client's arithmetic, in order. `keyBytes=*(u8*)(index+0x5e)`, `pageCount=*(i32*)(index+0x78)`, `cmpLen=min(keyBytes,keyLen)` computed once. The walk: `lo=0; hi=pageCount; page=0; while (lo != hi) { mid=(hi+lo)/2; cmp=memcmp(*(u64*)(index+0x88)+mid*keyBytes, key, cmpLen); if (cmp<0) lo=mid+1; else { hi=mid; if (cmp==0) { page=mid; break; } } } page=lo` after the loop. `page == pageCount` (which covers pageCount==0) and `page < 0` are the misses; status 6. Any other page calls CdnIndexPageResident (0x1424da590) and returns its non-zero status unchanged.

CdnIndexPageResident is NOT a unit of its own. Its measured function extent is 401 bytes, 0x1424da590..0x1424da721, and the whole-file path (0x1424da6ee..0x1424da705) is inside it - an earlier note said the whole-file path lay past a 82-byte .pdata root, which was a pre-merge measurement and is wrong; the merged register covers the whole body. It still cannot be a unit: it takes a lock-free pointer-computation path plus a streamed/HTTP path that needs the container, its I/O engine and a TLS-scoped lock object. Its whole-file expression is read and is staged here: `if (*(u8*)(index+0x38) == 0) { *(i32*)(index+0xa0)=page; *(u64*)(index+0x98)=*(u64*)(index+0x50) + (u32)(page * *(i32*)(index+0x6c)); return 0; }` — the product is a 32-bit IMUL zero-extended into the 64-bit add, and AL is cleared on both whole-file paths. The probe reproduces those two stores from the object's own fields and writes them back into the arena, so the unit compares the whole index object (including +0x98 and +0xa0) and a candidate that skipped the resident side effects diverges.

The record scan: `entriesPerPage=*(i32*)(index+0x74)`, `elementCount=*(i32*)(index+0x60)`, `count=min(entriesPerPage, elementCount - entriesPerPage*page)` in 32-bit wrapping arithmetic with an unsigned minimum, `entrySize=*(i32*)(index+0x70)`, `pageBase=*(u64*)(index+0x98)`; for `i in 0..count` the record is `pageBase + (u32)(entrySize*i)` and the first record whose `min(keyBytes,keyLen)` prefix matches wins (no equal-range expansion). The decode then writes `*out_size` (big-endian over `*(u8*)(index+0x5d)` bytes, accumulated in 32 bits, the slot zeroed first) and `*out_offset` (big-endian over `*(u8*)(index+0x5c)` bytes, accumulated in 64 bits, the slot zeroed first), and — before either — copies `min(keyBytes,16)` bytes of the RECORD into `out_key16` and zero-fills the rest to 16 when `out_key16` is non-null. Both out slots are written only on the found path; a miss, an empty count or a resident status leaves them untouched, which the fixture sees as its 0xA5 fill.

Return channel: AL. A found record returns `XOR AL,AL` (0) while RAX's upper bits still hold the last accumulated offset, a miss is `MOV AL,0x6`, and a resident status is returned as-is. The unit declares `returns: u8`, so the runner compares the low byte exactly and ignores the upper bits the client's callers ignore too.

Compared channels: the return, the whole index object (object fields, last-key array and page bodies, each of which the selector must not write), the 32-byte query buffer, and the three out slots. The resident's two stores at +0x98/+0xa0 are part of the object channel.

The fixture builds one arena buffer holding the object, the last-key array (+0x88) and the page bodies (+0x50), all as absolute arena addresses, and stores the buffer's own address at +0xa8 (a slot the selector never reads) so the probe can translate the pointers into offsets in its copy — the same plumbing fn/EncodingFindCKey uses at +0x68. Page bodies are `pageSize = 0x1000` bytes apart, records are `keyBytes + sizeWidth + offsetWidth` bytes, `entriesPerPage = pageSize / entrySize`, and the element count makes the last page partly filled as on a real index.

The pinned cases: a key on page 0, on the middle page and on the last page; a key at a page's first record; a key below every last key (page 0) and above the last key (status 6, both resident stores untouched); a key between two pages' last keys (the next page is selected and the scan misses); a key exactly equal to a page's last key (the early equal exit); two pages with the SAME last key, where the early exit answers the later page and a pure lower bound would answer the earlier one; duplicate records with one key (the first record wins); `key_len` shorter than the key width with the query's tail differing from the record's (the compare is `min(keyBytes,keyLen)` and the 16-byte copy comes from the record); `pageCount == 0`; a partly filled last page; a page with `count == 0`; the wrapping `elementCount - entriesPerPage*page`; offset widths 4/5/6/0; size width 4 and 0 (the size loop skipped); key widths 16 and 8 (the zero-fill copy path). The sweep after the specials varies page count 0..6, all widths, element counts and queries.

Coverage: the window is the whole 469-byte function, so all sixteen of its conditional branch sites are measured. Thirteen reach both edges with the corpus; three declare one dead edge, each validated by the coverage stage (site ran, exactly one edge observed, the declared edge never observed): the negative-page test, the resident non-zero-status test and the null-out_key16 test. 13/13 = 100%.

Mutation: the mutated body is select_page, the client's control-flow core (the loop, the three-way compare, the `lo`/`hi` update and the miss test). decode_page_record's scan and decode lines are not mutated by this unit — one mutation target per unit — but every case compares their three outputs (out_offset, out_size, out_key16) plus the object and the status, and the corpus gives every record a distinct size, a distinct offset and a distinct ordinal, so a decode defect shows up on the first divergent case. This is a declared gap, not a silent one.

allowedImageReads: 0x7ff7c87e5f40-0x7ff7c87e5f4f is the /GS security cookie at exe 0x143ac5f40, which CdnIndexPageResident (0x1424da590) reads and re-xors in its epilogue; 0x7ff7c8339480-0x7ff7c83395d4 is the CRT's memcpy/memset partial-block dispatch block at exe 0x143619480 (dword jump-offset tables, the same block fn/ApplyMoverSettings declares). They are fixed image data read by the stack check and the byte-copy helpers, not game state. The measured run reports exactly these ranges: 0x7ff7c83394a0+4, 0x7ff7c8339550+4 and 0x7ff7c87e5f40+8.

Relations: the page reader 0x1424d9af0 is fn/CdnIndexFooterParse; the batch wrapper CdnIndexPageSelectBatch (0x1424da910), CdnIndexPageResident (0x1424da590), the caller CdnResolveLocation (0x1424b0cc0) and the CDN config wiring are outside this unit.

acknowledgedGaps.why: The unit's object is always whole-file (`+0x38 == 0`), the branch ow-casc implements. The streamed branch builds an HTTP range request through the container's vtable and I/O engine, checks the page against its stored MD5 and needs the container object, its TLS-scoped lock and the extra scratch page; the oracle takes plain buffers and cannot build that state, and the port does not implement it. `decode_page_record` and `select_page` are branch-independent of it, and the coverage stage's second declaration pins that the resident never returns a non-zero status in this unit.

acknowledgedGaps.what: A `key_len` that makes the client's memcmp read past the query buffer
acknowledgedGaps.why: The client passes `min(keyBytes,keyLen)` to memcmp without checking the key buffer, so a key_len above the buffer's length reads whatever follows it. The fixture keeps `key_len <= 16 <= keyBytes` in the 32-byte query buffer and the probe refuses a longer one, so no case depends on the bytes past the buffer.

acknowledgedGaps.what: A page body shorter than the records the footer describes
acknowledgedGaps.why: The client computes `pageBase + entrySize*i` and reads without a bound. The fixture always supplies `pageSize` bytes per page and the probe slices what the resident pointer names; decode_page_record returns a miss for a record it cannot read inside the supplied body rather than reading past it, so a fault is not a behaviour here.

The mutation stage rewrites one function body per unit, and it is select_page (the search). The scan and decode are compared on every case through out_offset, out_size, out_key16, the object and the status, and the corpus separates every record's size, offset and ordinal, but no mutant of decode_page_record is generated, so the mutation kill rate does not measure that function directly.
